about: The catalog fixer's limits, field names and stock words. scripts/catalog_fix_plan.py reads this file, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.max_changes_per_batch: At most this many item updates go into one batch, which the user confirms with one yes. Deletes are always a batch of one.
notes.max_changes_per_plan: At most this many ready changes go into one plan; the rest are listed in deferred, for the next plan. Blocked and unchanged items don't count.
notes.import_min_items: When use_import_for_v2 (or --use-import) is on, a v2 batch of at least this many updates is written with one import_catalog_items call (each operation carrying the item's full record) instead of one upsert_catalog_item call per item. v1 catalogs always use upsert_catalog_item.
notes.protected_field_pattern: Regular expression (case-insensitive) for internal commercial fields: margin, cost, supplier, purchase, buy and landed prices and similar. A fix that touches a matching field is blocked, their values are kept unchanged in every payload, and they are never shown.
notes.id_case_insensitive: Match item IDs from the parity output and the change file to the saved items after trimming and lower-casing them. Must equal catalog-parity-check's value; a test checks it. The payload always uses the item's own ID.
notes.truncated_value_chars: catalog-parity-check cuts text values off at this many characters (str(v)[:200] in catalog_parity.py's display()); the two must match, and a test checks it. A Discovery URL, image or title this long may be cut off, so its fix is skipped until the user gives the full value.
notes.sparse_item_min_share: Warn when an item holds fewer than this share of the fields the catalog defines: an earlier partial write may have wiped it, and the update can only keep what is there.
notes.stock_out_number: The value written to a numeric stock field (stock_level and similar) to mark an item out of stock. Marking one in stock needs a quantity from the user.
notes.readback_checks: After each batch, read each item back up to this many times, a few seconds apart, while it still shows the old values (v1 writes are queued; v2 writes finish when their job succeeds), then run verify.
notes.default_engagement_fields: For each parity check, the Engagement properties that may hold the value, in order. Used when the parity output doesn't name the field: the first one the item holds, else the first one the catalog defines. --field NAME=EFIELD overrides one for a run. Must equal catalog-parity-check's fields[name].engagement lists; a test checks it.
notes.stock_text_pairs: In-stock and out-of-stock words that go together, lower-case. A text stock field is switched to the other word of the first pair that holds its value, keeping upper, title or first-letter case, so the catalog's vocabulary doesn't change. The extra pairs cover catalog-parity-check's other stock words: "low stock", "limited availability", "preorder" and "backorder" become "out of stock", and "sold out" becomes "in stock". A value in no pair ("discontinued", say) blocks the fix until the user gives the value.
notes.use_import_for_v2: Off until a live test confirms import_catalog_items' operation shape ({op: upsert, path: /<item_id>, value: {fields: ...}}): every update is then one upsert_catalog_item call. --use-import turns it on for a run; the first import batch is then one item, verified before the rest.
